reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) supports the general mechanism of coercivity enhancement via exchange bias and its temperature dependence, but it concerns entropy-stabilized oxide AFM layers on a Py FM layer, not a metallic HEA. The key premise that FeCoCrNiMn is ferromagnetic and can form an exchange-biased interface with NiO or FeMn is not supported by the cited passages, nor is the feasibility of depositing a well-adhered AFM on this specific HEA.
premises: Exchange bias at an FM/AFM interface can increase coercivity via domain wall pinning.
A thin AFM coating (e.g., NiO) can be deposited on a metallic substrate to form an FM/AFM interface.
The FeCoCrNiMn HEA is ferromagnetic and can act as the FM layer in an exchange bias system.
The exchange bias effect and coercivity enhancement vanish above the AFM's blocking/Néel temperature.
Chemical disorder in high-entropy materials can enhance interface exchange coupling.
